verdict.rationale: smolagents exposes the agent's memory (docs-21) and lets callbacks modify it (docs-8). It also supports running an agent one step at a time, which the docs pitch for long-running tool calls (docs-9, docs-17), and replaying a run with agent.replay() (docs-7). Together these are primitives a developer could use to build checkpointing by hand, but nothing in the evidence shows built-in persistence of agent state or resuming after a crash. Missing for 10: built-in serialization of agent state/memory to durable storage, a documented resume-from-checkpoint API after a crash or restart, and hands-on or independent confirmation that a run resumes exactly where it left off.
